body:
Five-minute poll. One item was actionable and it turned into the thing that put it in front
of me being wrong.

PR #2009 (BUG-1420) — CHANGES REQUESTED recorded at 065f3df8aa. Do not merge.

I picked it up because `aida awaiting` listed it under mergeable_prs with ci_rollup "pass".
It is not green. The head has exactly ONE check-run:

    gh api repos/joemooney/aida/commits/065f3df8aa/check-runs
      merge-hold-gate: completed / success
      (no Build row)

Build (ubuntu-latest) — required for main — never ran on that commit. awaiting's own doc
comment says ci_rollup is pass "when every check is green", meaning every check that EXISTS,
with no concept of which are REQUIRED. So a head carrying one trivial green check and no
build is indistinguishable from a fully-passing pipeline, and gets surfaced to a seat as
ready.

Filed BUG-1481, high. It is BUG-1466's shape again and I said so in the spec: there the drain
matches only on Approved and never compares reviewed_sha, so an approval authorizes any head;
here awaiting matches only the checks present and never asks which are required, so an
incomplete pipeline reads as a complete one. Both compute a green from an incomplete set.
Neither notices ABSENCE. I wrote the acceptance so a missing required check reads as NOT-green,
mirroring your own addition to BUG-1466 that the gate must refuse on a MISSING sha rather than
only a mismatched one — same rule, two surfaces, and they should not get two ad-hoc fixes.

One note on its test coverage, in the form you asked me to start using: every existing test in
awaiting_you.rs builds PRs through a helper that passes Some("pass") straight in. They assert
the CLASSIFIER given a rollup and never exercise how the rollup is DERIVED. The defect is
upstream of every current test, so no assertion added to them would reach it.

THE REST OF #2009, briefly. 12 commits carrying 9 specs on a PR titled for one; 25 commits
behind main; 7 of the 9 already landed on main via other PRs (BUG-1279 #1991, SPIKE-83 #2004,
TASK-1290, TASK-1297, BUG-1277, BUG-1298, TASK-1292 — shas on the verdict). Only TASK-1289 and
BUG-1420 are not on main. A 39-file / 4369-insertion diff for a spec whose own text calls it a
self-contained change to one subprocess spawn.

THE BUG-1420 CODE ITSELF IS GOOD and I recorded that prominently so a rebase does not lose it.
github_actions_bash spawns --noprofile --norc -e -o pipefail, and AC2/AC3 are met the way the
spec specifically demanded — behavioural tests (first command fails and last succeeds must
fail; `false | true` must fail) rather than argv assertions, which the spec warned would pass
even if the shell ignored the flags. Cherry-pick 065f3df8aa onto a fresh branch off main and it
ships. AC4 is partially met (documented, but nothing DETECTS drift, which is what its second
sentence asks for) and AC5 shows no evidence of the guard audit — and the spec comment already
predicts the CLI-manual guard will fail under the stricter shell for an unrelated reason
(TASK-1-152), which IS the AC5 case and should be recorded now rather than discovered next round.

ONE THING I DID DELIBERATELY. A verdict at this same head already existed with two findings,
and a later spec comment disputes both as stale-base artifacts — the BUG-1277 test is correct on
main, and the SPIKE-83 whitespace is intentional markdown. Since verdict files are overwritten
each round (STORY-1391), a later reader of the verdict alone would action two wrong findings. I
carried the dispute INTO the new verdict as its own finding rather than letting it live only in
a comment. That is your rule from this morning applied in the direction you did not state it:
not only must a finding not live solely in a verdict file, a REFUTATION must not live solely
outside one.

-- reviewer (claude-reviewer-1)
